You are BIE's book-understanding section: an expert teacher of Indian Economy for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS.
You read one page of a book chapter with two eyes, the page's native text blocks and the page image, and turn it into a complete,
question-based teacher's understanding. Later BIE sections build the video lessons, the chapter game and the notes only from what you
capture, so anything you miss is missing from the whole course. Your output is internal to BIE: write it in clear English and keep the
book's own terms and spellings.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.
[S1-02] Every native text block is either covered by an item (its id in that item's block_ids) or listed as boilerplate. Boilerplate is only running headers, page numbers, publisher adverts, contact lines and watermarks; nothing teachable is boilerplate.
[S1-03] Every table becomes one 'table' item plus one 'table_row' item per row, in order, each row's content giving every cell with its column header, for example 'Smooth muscle | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary'. A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.
[S1-04] Every diagram, chart, flow or tree becomes one 'diagram' item that says what it shows and how its parts connect (arrows, branches, flows, sequence), plus one 'diagram_label' item per label naming what the label points to. A classification tree lists every branch and leaf with its parent.
[S1-05] Every equation, formula, chemical formula and symbol is read exactly and each symbol's meaning and unit are stated.
[S1-06] Understand every teachable item by questioning it like a teacher. Ask the questions that fit: what is it, what is it about, where does it apply or occur, how does it work, when, who and whom, which, why, how does it compare, how does it differ, what is the evidence, what are the exceptions, what follows from it. Then keep asking 'why' and 'how' on your own answers (depth 2, 3 ...) until a teacher could explain it to a student meeting it for the first time. Answers explain; they never just repeat the item's words.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-08] Give every item its true content type, one of BIE's nine: process, structure, classification, comparison, timeline, cause_effect, facts_numbers, figure, definition (bie/brain/rulebook/content_types.json). An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a question or an answer option is a role, not a type. BIE's code proposes a type before you read the page; when you choose another, say why. The content type decides the required questions and later how the lesson teaches it, how the video shows it, how the game makes it playable and how the notes draw it, so choose by what the content is, not by how it is printed.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.
[S1-10] Judge exam importance for the course's exam (for UPSC / State PCS: classifications, comparisons, locations, functions, examples and odd-one-out facts are high). Every previous-year or practice question on the page is captured with its options and linked to the items it tests.
[S1-11] Where the text layer and the image disagree (garbled symbols, missing words, wrong order), report the disagreement. Trust the image for symbols, layout and diagrams, and the text layer for spelling when it is clean.
[S1-13] A printed typo stays as printed, with the right word after it in square brackets: 'Cartiage [Cartilage]' (Navin, 23 October 2026). The teacher answers use the right word. Never correct the book silently.
[S1-14] One answer, one basis (Navin, 23 October 2026): an answer that would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one with basis 'book' (only what the page states) and one with basis 'outside'.
[S1-15] Open every teachable item for the learner (Navin, 24 October 2026): in unpack, the terms the learner must hold (each with its plain meaning in simple Hindi and one everyday image), a why chain of 1-4 steps that starts from a need or a problem (each step names its basis, book or standard), an example or the place where it is seen, the consequence, the visual verb the video should show, and what the level profile adds. Every teachable item has at least one unpack element; an unpack that only restates the item in other words is empty.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.
- text_image_disagreements: where the text layer and the image differ.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

items.content: A cheque is a special type of bill of exchange drawn on a bank and payable on demand.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes a cheque in this definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a bill of exchange directed to a bank, with payment due on demand rather than at a stated future maturity.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words identify the paying institution and timing?
teacher_understanding.answer: ‘Drawn on a bank’ identifies the institution; ‘payable on demand’ identifies when payment is due.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a beginner understand ‘drawn on’?
teacher_understanding.answer: The account holder gives a written payment instruction to the bank. It does not mean the cheque itself is currency or that payment is unconditional.

items.exam_note: Distinguish a bank-directed payment instruction from cash and from a prepaid demand draft.

terms.everyday_image: दुकानदार cheque को अपने bank में जमा करता है

terms.plain_meaning: एक व्यक्ति का दूसरे को तय रकम चुकाने का लिखित आदेश
terms.everyday_image: लिखी हुई पर्ची में किसी को पैसे देने का आदेश

why_chain.step: A person needs to pay through a bank account without handing over cash.
A cheque directs the bank to pay and is payable on demand.

unpack.example_or_place: A customer gives a cheque to a supplier.
unpack.consequence: Payment depends on the bank honouring the instruction, linking to dishonour below.
unpack.visual_verb: send a written instruction from account holder to bank
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret payable on demand as a guarantee of successful payment.

items.content: Parties involved: Drawer (account holder), Drawee (bank), Payee

teacher_understanding.question: What parties make up the cheque relationship?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page names the drawer as account holder, the drawee as bank, and the payee as the third party.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does each party stand in a payment instruction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawer issues the instruction, the drawee bank is instructed to pay, and the payee is the person to whom payment is directed.

teacher_understanding.question: How can these easily confused names be separated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Ask three different questions: who writes the cheque, which bank must pay, and who receives the payment.

items.exam_note: Role-matching questions can interchange drawer and drawee.

terms.plain_meaning: cheque लिखकर भुगतान का आदेश देने वाला
terms.everyday_image: खरीदार cheque पर हस्ताक्षर करता है

terms.plain_meaning: वह bank जिसे भुगतान का आदेश दिया गया है
terms.everyday_image: cheque पर लिखा bank का नाम

terms.plain_meaning: जिसे रकम मिलनी है
terms.everyday_image: दुकानदार के नाम बना cheque

why_chain.step: A cheque separates the person ordering payment from the institution making payment.
Separate role names prevent confusion about who gives, executes and receives the instruction.

unpack.example_or_place: A buyer writes a cheque on their bank in favour of a seller.
unpack.consequence: The drawer's failure to provide funds becomes relevant to dishonour.
unpack.visual_verb: connect drawer, bank and payee
unpack.level_extra: Practise matching roles rather than memorising names in isolation.

items.content: Section 138: Cheque dishonour: A cheque is dishonoured for reasons such as insufficient funds, and the drawer does not make payment after receiving the statutory demand notice. Makes cheque bouncing a criminal offence
items.type_note: The passage links dishonour and non-payment after notice to a criminal consequence; it is not principally a staged process.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page connect cheque bouncing with a criminal offence?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its Section 138 account combines dishonour, such as for insufficient funds, with the drawer's failure to pay after receiving the statutory demand notice.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the demand notice fit into this explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The notice precedes the non-payment identified by the page; the passage does not simply say that every returned cheque immediately creates a criminal offence.

teacher_understanding.question: What does ‘statutory demand notice’ mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a formal demand for payment required by the applicable law, rather than merely an informal reminder.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this short paragraph not be treated as the complete legal test?
teacher_understanding.answer: Section 138 has additional legal requirements, including a legally enforceable debt or liability and prescribed procedural conditions. The page is an introductory summary.

items.exam_note: Keep insufficient funds, notice and subsequent non-payment together; avoid ‘every bounce is automatically criminal’.

terms.everyday_image: जमा किया cheque बिना भुगतान लौट आता है

कानून के मुताबिक भेजी गई भुगतान की औपचारिक माँग
terms.everyday_image: रकम चुकाने के लिए लिखित कानूनी notice

why_chain.step: A payee expecting payment may instead receive an unpaid cheque.
The page links dishonour and failure to pay after statutory notice with a criminal consequence under Section 138.

unpack.example_or_place: A seller receives a cheque that is returned for insufficient funds.
unpack.consequence: A cheque is a payment instruction, not a bank-guaranteed prepaid instrument like the demand draft described next.
unpack.visual_verb: return cheque, deliver notice, show continued non-payment
unpack.level_extra: Section 138 belongs to the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (standard outside context); no legal deadlines are supplied on this page.

items.content: Demand Draft and Overdraft Facilities

items.where_on_page: under Demand Draft and Overdraft Facilities
items.content: Demand Draft

items.where_on_page: upper middle, first two Demand Draft bullets
items.content: It is a prepaid payment instrument issued by a bank. To transfer money securely.

teacher_understanding.question: What is a demand draft and what is its purpose?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a bank-issued payment instrument paid for in advance and used to transfer money securely.

teacher_understanding.question: Which word distinguishes its funding from an ordinary cheque?
teacher_understanding.answer: ‘Prepaid’ states that funding occurs before the draft is issued, rather than relying on the drawer's account when a cheque is presented.

teacher_understanding.question: How does prepayment help the recipient?
teacher_understanding.answer: The bank has already received the amount and guarantees the payment, as the next bullet explains.

items.exam_note: Bank-issued and prepaid are the defining combination.

terms.plain_meaning: पहले रकम देकर लिया गया
terms.everyday_image: पहले recharge, फिर सेवा का इस्तेमाल

terms.plain_meaning: पहले पैसा लेकर bank का जारी किया भुगतान का साधन
terms.everyday_image: फीस जमा करने के लिए bank से draft बनवाना

why_chain.step: A recipient needs a secure way to receive money.
A bank issues a prepaid instrument for that transfer.

unpack.example_or_place: A bank demand draft used for an institution's fee payment.
unpack.consequence: Prepayment explains the bank guarantee in the next item.
unpack.visual_verb: pay bank first, then issue draft
unpack.level_extra: Contrast funding before issuance with a cheque's dependence on payment being honoured.

items.where_on_page: upper middle, wrapped Demand Draft bullet
items.content: The payment is guaranteed by the bank because the customer pays the amount to the bank before the draft is issued.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the bank guarantee a demand draft's payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: The customer has already paid the amount to the bank before issuance, so the guarantee rests on money already received.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the funding order important?
teacher_understanding.answer: Customer payment comes first and draft issuance follows; the bank is not waiting for the customer to arrange the amount after the draft is presented.

items.exam_note: The bank guarantee follows prepayment; it is not a loan to the purchaser.

terms.plain_meaning: भुगतान की जिम्मेदारी bank लेता है
terms.everyday_image: रकम पहले अपने पास लेकर bank भुगतान का भरोसा देता है

why_chain.step: The recipient wants assurance that the amount will be available.
The customer pays before issuance, allowing the bank to guarantee payment.

unpack.example_or_place: A purchaser pays the draft amount at the bank before receiving the draft.
unpack.consequence: Demand draft funding is the opposite of the credit facility introduced below.
unpack.visual_verb: move money into bank before stamping the draft
unpack.level_extra: Separate secure payment from credit creation for the customer.

items.content: Overdraft Facility:
It is a short-term credit facility that allows a customer to withdraw more money than is available in their bank account.

teacher_understanding.question: What does an overdraft allow?
teacher_understanding.answer: It permits withdrawals beyond the customer's available bank balance through short-term credit.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words show that the extra amount is not the customer's own deposit?
teacher_understanding.answer: ‘Credit facility’ identifies borrowing, while ‘more money than is available’ separates that borrowing from the existing balance.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a customer withdraw beyond their own money?
teacher_understanding.answer: The bank authorises borrowing up to a limit; the amount used beyond the balance becomes an obligation to repay.

items.exam_note: Overdraft is credit, not an increase in the customer's own deposit.

terms.plain_meaning: खाते में अपने पैसे से ज्यादा रकम निकालने की bank की मंजूरी
terms.everyday_image: खाते की रकम खत्म होने पर मंजूर सीमा तक उधार इस्तेमाल करना

terms.plain_meaning: कम अवधि की जरूरत के लिए लिया उधार
terms.everyday_image: कमाई आने से पहले जरूरी खर्च पूरा करना

why_chain.step: A customer may face a temporary gap between a payment due and money available.
An overdraft allows withdrawal beyond the available balance through short-term credit.

unpack.example_or_place: A small trader pays a bill before customer receipts arrive.
unpack.consequence: The extra withdrawal is borrowed money; the diagram shows its limit and interest treatment.
unpack.visual_verb: extend withdrawal beyond the balance marker
unpack.level_extra: Contrast prepaid demand draft with borrowed overdraft funds.

items.content: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, eligible account holders may receive an overdraft facility

teacher_understanding.question: Which scheme is linked to an overdraft facility?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page links Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana with the possibility of an overdraft for eligible account holders.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words prevent treating it as an automatic benefit for every holder?
teacher_understanding.answer: ‘Eligible’ and ‘may receive’ make the statement conditional rather than universal.

teacher_understanding.question: Why connect an account-opening initiative with credit access?
teacher_understanding.answer: Financial inclusion involves usable financial services, including access to small credit needs, not merely possessing an account.

items.exam_note: Do not infer a PMJDY overdraft amount from the unrelated ₹40,000 illustration.

terms.plain_meaning: वे खाताधारक जो तय शर्तें पूरी करते हैं
terms.everyday_image: फॉर्म में जरूरी शर्तों पर सही निशान लगना

why_chain.step: Having an account may not meet a household's temporary shortage of money.
The page identifies a possible overdraft facility for eligible PMJDY account holders.

unpack.example_or_place: An eligible Jan Dhan account holder seeking short-term credit.
unpack.consequence: Access is conditional; the page supplies no scheme-specific limit.
unpack.visual_verb: filter account holders through eligibility
unpack.level_extra: Statement questions may replace ‘eligible’ with ‘all’.

items.content: A right-pointing arrow connects ‘Account Balance ₹10,000’ on the left to ‘OD Limit ₹40,000’ on the right. Beneath them: ‘You can withdraw up to ₹50,000 in total.’ and ‘Interest applies only to the overdraft amount used.’ The figure combines own balance and an authorised overdraft limit; the arrow does not show an actual ₹40,000 withdrawal.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this overdraft illustration show?
teacher_understanding.answer: With ₹10,000 in the account and a ₹40,000 overdraft limit, the illustrated total withdrawal capacity is ₹50,000.

teacher_understanding.question: Which amount attracts interest according to the figure?
teacher_understanding.answer: The overdraft actually used, not the entire available overdraft limit.

teacher_understanding.question: How would a ₹25,000 withdrawal illustrate the distinction?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this simplified example, ₹10,000 comes from the customer's balance and ₹15,000 is overdraft used. The interest-bearing overdraft amount would be ₹15,000, not ₹40,000 or ₹25,000.

items.exam_note: Separate own balance, sanctioned limit, total availability and actual borrowing.

terms.plain_meaning: overdraft से उधार लेने की मंजूर अधिकतम सीमा
terms.everyday_image: उधार की छत, पूरी रकम लेना जरूरी नहीं

why_chain.step: A customer needs to know both spending capacity and borrowing cost.
The figure adds own funds to the limit but attaches interest only to overdraft used.

unpack.example_or_place: ₹10,000 balance + ₹40,000 OD limit = ₹50,000 illustrated availability.
unpack.consequence: An unused credit limit is not the same as a loan already drawn.
unpack.visual_verb: stack own funds and available credit, then highlight only credit used
unpack.level_extra: Use a simple numerical scenario without inventing an interest rate.

items.content: Account Balance ₹10,000 — left box showing the customer's existing account balance.

teacher_understanding.question: What does ₹10,000 represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the account balance shown before the overdraft is added to the illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Which part is not overdraft credit?
teacher_understanding.answer: The ₹10,000 account balance is separate from the ₹40,000 OD limit.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this amount be mentally separated from borrowing?
teacher_understanding.answer: Treat it as the customer's own available funds, with borrowing beginning beyond that amount in the example.

items.exam_note: Own funds are not interest-bearing overdraft use.

terms.plain_meaning: खाते में मौजूद अपनी रकम
terms.everyday_image: passbook में दिखते ₹10,000

unpack.example_or_place: Left box in the overdraft illustration.
unpack.consequence: This amount contributes to total availability without being the OD limit.
unpack.visual_verb: fill own-money segment
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish deposit balance from credit availability.

items.content: OD Limit ₹40,000 — right box reached by the arrow from Account Balance.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the ₹40,000 label specify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It specifies the overdraft limit available in this illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Which is the credit component of the ₹50,000 capacity?
teacher_understanding.answer: The ₹40,000 OD limit, rather than the ₹10,000 account balance.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a limit differ from actual use?
teacher_understanding.answer: A limit authorises borrowing up to a ceiling; it does not mean the customer has borrowed that entire amount.

items.exam_note: Illustrative amount, not a stated universal or PMJDY limit.

unpack.example_or_place: Right box: ₹40,000 available credit.
unpack.consequence: Available credit can remain partly or wholly unused.
unpack.visual_verb: draw a credit ceiling
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse sanction with utilisation.

items.where_on_page: overdraft diagram, first line below boxes
items.content: You can withdraw up to ₹50,000 in total.

teacher_understanding.question: What total does the figure give?
teacher_understanding.answer: The illustrated maximum withdrawal capacity is ₹50,000.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two components produce this total?
teacher_understanding.answer: The ₹10,000 account balance and the ₹40,000 OD limit.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the total calculated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Add own balance and authorised overdraft: ₹10,000 + ₹40,000 = ₹50,000.

items.exam_note: Total availability is not total borrowing.

unpack.example_or_place: The combined capacity in the black illustration.
unpack.consequence: At the illustrated maximum withdrawal, only ₹40,000 comes from overdraft.
unpack.visual_verb: join two amount bars
unpack.level_extra: A simple arithmetic trap is to call ₹50,000 the OD limit.

items.content: Interest applies only to the overdraft amount used.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the stated interest rule?
teacher_understanding.answer: Interest attaches to the amount of overdraft used.

teacher_understanding.question: Which distinction controls this interest statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Actual utilisation is distinguished from the available ₹40,000 OD limit.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish usage from availability?
teacher_understanding.answer: Permission to borrow is different from receiving borrowed money; the figure bases interest on the latter.

items.exam_note: The statement concerns interest; do not infer that no other contractual charges can exist.

terms.plain_meaning: मंजूर उधार में से सच में इस्तेमाल की रकम

unpack.example_or_place: Only the drawn credit segment is highlighted for interest.
unpack.consequence: An unused portion is not included in the figure's interest base.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight used credit only
unpack.level_extra: No rate or time period is given, so no interest amount can be calculated.

items.content: Banking Codes

items.where_on_page: Banking Codes, MICR heading and first two sub-bullets
items.content: MICR code: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition. 9 digits code written in Iron Oxide ink for automated clearance.

teacher_understanding.question: What does MICR stand for, and what format does the page give?
teacher_understanding.answer: MICR means Magnetic Ink Character Recognition; the page describes a nine-digit code printed in Iron Oxide ink for automated clearance.

teacher_understanding.question: Which details distinguish MICR from IFSC on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: MICR has nine digits and special ink for automated cheque clearance, whereas IFSC has eleven alphanumeric characters for electronic branch identification.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the special ink help a machine read the code?
teacher_understanding.answer: Iron oxide gives the printed characters magnetic properties that suitable readers can detect, supporting machine recognition.

items.exam_note: Learn full form, nine digits and Iron Oxide ink; do not substitute the IFSC format.

terms.plain_meaning: खास magnetic ink के characters को machine से पहचानने का तरीका
terms.everyday_image: cheque के नीचे छपा code machine पढ़ती है

terms.plain_meaning: हर cheque की जानकारी हाथ से भरने के बजाय machine की मदद से भुगतान निपटाना
terms.everyday_image: cheques की गड्डी machine से गुजरती है

why_chain.step: Large numbers of paper cheques need dependable identification.
A nine-digit code in Iron Oxide ink supports automated clearance.

unpack.example_or_place: The machine-readable code line on a cheque.
unpack.consequence: The next bullet explains faster and more accurate cheque processing.
unpack.visual_verb: scan magnetic characters on a cheque
unpack.level_extra: MICR is numeric; IFSC is alphanumeric. Keep the two purposes separate.

items.content: It allows cheque-sorting machines to read and process cheques quickly and accurately.
items.type_note: The sentence states the functional effect of MICR, not stages or timing of cheque processing.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is MICR useful in cheque handling?
teacher_understanding.answer: It enables cheque-sorting machines to read and process cheques quickly and accurately.

teacher_understanding.question: How can machine-readable codes improve processing?
teacher_understanding.answer: Machines can capture standardised characters instead of relying on repeated manual reading and entry, reducing opportunities for transcription errors.

teacher_understanding.question: What operational consequence does the page emphasise?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both speed and accuracy improve; its stated benefit is not merely a distinctive appearance on the cheque.

items.exam_note: Match MICR with cheque sorting and processing, rather than electronic transfer routing.

terms.plain_meaning: cheques के code पढ़कर उन्हें छाँटने वाली machines
terms.everyday_image: बहुत-से कागज पढ़कर सही ढेर में रखना

why_chain.step: Reading many cheque details by hand is slow and can introduce errors.
MICR enables machines to read and process cheques quickly and accurately.

unpack.example_or_place: High-volume cheque processing in banking.
unpack.consequence: MICR solves a paper-cheque processing problem; IFSC addresses electronic destination identification.
unpack.visual_verb: sort a stream of cheques into correct routes
unpack.level_extra: Recognition, sorting and processing are linked functions, not a new payment app.

items.where_on_page: lower middle, IFSC heading and definition
items.content: Indian Financial System Code (IFSC): It is an 11-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies every bank branch participating in electronic payment systems.

teacher_understanding.question: What does IFSC identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies a participating bank branch in electronic payment systems through an eleven-character alphanumeric code.

teacher_understanding.question: Which wording rules out calling IFSC an eleven-digit account number?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says ‘11-character alphanumeric’ and specifies identification of a bank branch, not an individual account.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must electronic transfers identify the branch accurately?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank can have many branches; the transfer system needs an unambiguous destination rather than just a bank name.

items.exam_note: Eleven characters, alphanumeric, branch identifier—not a personal account number.

terms.plain_meaning: अक्षर और अंक मिलाकर बना
terms.everyday_image: घर के पते जैसा A-12

terms.plain_meaning: electronic payment में bank branch पहचानने वाला code
terms.everyday_image: डाक के पते में सही जगह की पहचान

why_chain.step: Electronic money needs a precise branch destination.
IFSC uniquely identifies participating branches with an eleven-character code.

unpack.example_or_place: A bank-transfer beneficiary form asking for IFSC.
unpack.consequence: Correct branch identification supports the transfers listed next.
unpack.visual_verb: match code to one branch
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse branch identification with identifying the beneficiary's individual account.

items.content: IFSC is required for: NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS payments. It ensures that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page associate IFSC with electronic transfers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its stated role is to ensure that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: How does IFSC support the named payment systems?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies the branch identifier used to route a transfer to the intended branch.

teacher_understanding.question: Which payment systems are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT, RTGS and IMPS are listed as requiring IFSC.

teacher_understanding.question: Should this be read as a requirement to manually enter IFSC in every possible IMPS interface?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. IMPS also supports mobile-number-and-MMID addressing. The page's statement fits the account-number-and-IFSC route and should not be generalised to every interface.

items.exam_note: Preserve the book's system list, but distinguish branch routing from a universal manual-entry rule.

terms.everyday_image: एक ही नाम की कई दुकानों में सही दुकान चुनना

why_chain.step: An electronic instruction must distinguish its destination branch.
The page links IFSC with correct electronic branch delivery for NEFT, RTGS and IMPS.

unpack.consequence: Code-based routing links bank identifiers to the wider digital-payment arrangement below.

items.where_on_page: bottom left, narrow column beside diagram
items.content: RBI is the apex authority for payment and settlement systems under the Payment and Settlement

teacher_understanding.question: What authority does the page assign to RBI?
teacher_understanding.answer: RBI is the apex authority for payment and settlement systems.

teacher_understanding.question: What on this page reinforces RBI's top-level role?
teacher_understanding.answer: The adjacent diagram places Reserve Bank of India at the top and labels it ‘Regulator • Oversees settlement systems’.

replace_items.content: IFSC is required for: NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS payments. It ensures that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page associate IFSC with electronic transfers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its stated role is to ensure that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: How does IFSC support the named payment systems?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies the branch identifier used to route a transfer to the intended branch.

teacher_understanding.question: Which payment systems are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT, RTGS and IMPS are listed as requiring IFSC.

teacher_understanding.question: What is NEFT, and where would a customer use it?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT means National Electronic Funds Transfer. It transfers funds electronically between bank accounts, for example when a tenant sends rent to a landlord. Transactions are settled in half-hourly batches, and the system operates round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How does NEFT's batch settlement work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Payment instructions are grouped for a settlement cycle rather than each instruction being settled separately as soon as it arrives. A customer's electronic submission can therefore be immediate even though interbank settlement follows the batch cycle.

teacher_understanding.question: What is RTGS, and what familiar need does it serve?
teacher_understanding.answer: RTGS means Real Time Gross Settlement. It settles transfers individually in real time rather than grouping them into batches or netting them against other transfers. It is used for large-value payments, such as a substantial property payment; its minimum transaction amount is ₹2 lakh, and the system operates round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How do 'real time' and 'gross' describe different aspects of RTGS?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Real time' concerns timing: processing occurs as instructions are received rather than waiting for a batch. 'Gross' concerns the settlement unit: each transaction is settled individually for its full amount.

teacher_understanding.question: What is IMPS, and when might a household use it?
teacher_understanding.answer: IMPS means Immediate Payment Service. It provides immediate interbank electronic transfers round the clock, including holidays. A person could use mobile or internet banking to send urgent money to a family member.

teacher_understanding.question: What basic distinction separates NEFT, RTGS and IMPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT uses batch settlement; RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time and is intended for large-value transfers; IMPS provides immediate customer transfers. Immediate customer credit under IMPS should not be equated with RTGS-style transaction-wise gross interbank settlement. All three offer round-the-clock service, so availability alone does not distinguish them.

teacher_understanding.question: Should the book's statement be read as requiring manual IFSC entry in every possible IMPS interface?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. IMPS also supports mobile-number-and-MMID addressing. The page's statement fits the account-number-and-IFSC route and should not be generalised to every interface.

replace_items.exam_note: Distinguish NEFT batches, RTGS real-time gross settlement and IMPS immediate transfers. Round-the-clock availability is not unique to IMPS. Preserve the IFSC list without assuming universal manual entry.

teacher_understanding.question: Which systems must be retained from this image-only list?
teacher_understanding.answer: All five names—UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS and NACH—belong to the NPCI box.

teacher_understanding.question: How does NPCI differ from RBI in this diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: NPCI is assigned operation of named systems; RBI is assigned regulation and settlement-system oversight.

teacher_understanding.question: What does NPCI stand for?
teacher_understanding.answer: National Payments Corporation of India.

teacher_understanding.question: What is UPI, and how does a consumer encounter it?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI means Unified Payments Interface. It enables instant bank-account payments through participating apps, for example by scanning a shop's QR code or using a UPI ID. The app is the interface; UPI is the shared payment arrangement connecting participating institutions.

teacher_understanding.question: What is IMPS, and how is it used?
teacher_understanding.answer: IMPS means Immediate Payment Service. It enables immediate interbank transfers round the clock, such as sending urgent money to a relative through mobile or internet banking. Account number with IFSC is one addressing route; mobile number with MMID is another.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should UPI and IMPS not be treated as identical names for one app?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both support immediate transfers, but they are distinct NPCI services. UPI offers app-based payment initiation using features such as UPI IDs and QR codes; IMPS is a transfer service commonly accessed through bank channels. Neither name denotes just one commercial app.

teacher_understanding.question: What is RuPay, and where is it seen?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay is India's domestic card payment network. A bank can issue a RuPay debit, credit or prepaid card for transactions such as paying at a shop, making an online purchase or using an ATM. RuPay identifies the card network, not the bank account or a particular bank.

teacher_understanding.question: What is AePS, and what problem does it help solve?
teacher_understanding.answer: AePS means Aadhaar Enabled Payment System. It supports basic banking transactions using Aadhaar authentication for an Aadhaar-linked account. For example, a person can withdraw cash through a business correspondent's micro-ATM using supported biometric authentication, without visiting a regular bank branch.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the familiar AePS cash-withdrawal example work?
teacher_understanding.answer: The customer identifies the Aadhaar-linked banking relationship and authenticates at the correspondent's device. After authorisation, the account is debited and the correspondent hands over cash. Aadhaar helps identify and authenticate the transaction; it is not itself an account holding the money.

teacher_understanding.question: What is NACH, and where is it used?
teacher_understanding.answer: NACH means National Automated Clearing House. It supports bulk electronic credits and debits, including periodic payments. Examples include salary or pension credits to many accounts and authorised recurring debits for insurance premiums or loan instalments.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use NACH rather than manually initiate every recurring payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: An institution may need to pay many people or collect repeated payments from many customers. Bulk processing reduces repeated individual instructions; recurring debits operate under customer authorisation through a mandate, not unrestricted permission to take money.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the five systems be distinguished by familiar uses?
teacher_understanding.answer: Think of UPI for app-based instant payments, IMPS for immediate bank transfers, RuPay for card transactions, AePS for Aadhaar-authenticated basic banking, and NACH for bulk or recurring credits and debits. These are distinguishing functions, not rigidly exclusive use categories.

replace_items.exam_note: Match both operator and function. AePS is Aadhaar-authenticated banking, RuPay is a card network, and NACH handles bulk credits as well as debits; do not reduce every NPCI service to a UPI app.

items.content: A cheque is a special type of bill of exchange drawn on a bank and payable on demand.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes a cheque in this definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a bill of exchange directed to a bank, with payment due on demand rather than at a stated future maturity.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words identify the paying institution and timing?
teacher_understanding.answer: ‘Drawn on a bank’ identifies the institution; ‘payable on demand’ identifies when payment is due.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a beginner understand ‘drawn on’?
teacher_understanding.answer: The account holder gives a written payment instruction to the bank. It does not mean the cheque itself is currency or that payment is unconditional.

items.content: IFSC is required for: NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS payments. It ensures that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page associate IFSC with electronic transfers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its stated role is to ensure that money reaches the correct bank branch electronically.

teacher_understanding.question: How does IFSC support the named payment systems?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies the branch identifier used to route a transfer to the intended branch.

teacher_understanding.question: Which payment systems are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT, RTGS and IMPS are listed as requiring IFSC.

teacher_understanding.question: What is NEFT, and where would a customer use it?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT means National Electronic Funds Transfer. It transfers funds electronically between bank accounts, for example when a tenant sends rent to a landlord. Transactions are settled in half-hourly batches, and the system operates round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How does NEFT's batch settlement work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Payment instructions are grouped for a settlement cycle rather than each instruction being settled separately as soon as it arrives. A customer's electronic submission can therefore be immediate even though interbank settlement follows the batch cycle.

teacher_understanding.question: What is RTGS, and what familiar need does it serve?
teacher_understanding.answer: RTGS means Real Time Gross Settlement. It settles transfers individually in real time rather than grouping them into batches or netting them against other transfers. It is used for large-value payments, such as a substantial property payment; its minimum transaction amount is ₹2 lakh, and the system operates round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How do 'real time' and 'gross' describe different aspects of RTGS?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Real time' concerns timing: processing occurs as instructions are received rather than waiting for a batch. 'Gross' concerns the settlement unit: each transaction is settled individually for its full amount.

teacher_understanding.question: What is IMPS, and when might a household use it?
teacher_understanding.answer: IMPS means Immediate Payment Service. It provides immediate interbank electronic transfers round the clock, including holidays. A person could use mobile or internet banking to send urgent money to a family member.

teacher_understanding.question: What basic distinction separates NEFT, RTGS and IMPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT uses batch settlement; RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time and is intended for large-value transfers; IMPS provides immediate customer transfers. Immediate customer credit under IMPS should not be equated with RTGS-style transaction-wise gross interbank settlement. All three offer round-the-clock service, so availability alone does not distinguish them.

teacher_understanding.question: Should the book's statement be read as requiring manual IFSC entry in every possible IMPS interface?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. IMPS also supports mobile-number-and-MMID addressing. The page's statement fits the account-number-and-IFSC route and should not be generalised to every interface.

items.exam_note: Distinguish NEFT batches, RTGS real-time gross settlement and IMPS immediate transfers. Round-the-clock availability is not unique to IMPS. Preserve the IFSC list without assuming universal manual entry.

items.content: NPCI — Runs UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS, NACH

teacher_understanding.question: What role does the NPCI box state?
teacher_understanding.answer: NPCI runs the listed systems: UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS and NACH.

teacher_understanding.question: Which systems must be retained from this image-only list?
teacher_understanding.answer: All five names—UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS and NACH—belong to the NPCI box.

teacher_understanding.question: How does NPCI differ from RBI in this diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: NPCI is assigned operation of named systems; RBI is assigned regulation and settlement-system oversight.

teacher_understanding.question: What does NPCI stand for?
teacher_understanding.answer: National Payments Corporation of India.

teacher_understanding.question: What is UPI, and how does a consumer encounter it?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI means Unified Payments Interface. It enables instant bank-account payments through participating apps, for example by scanning a shop's QR code or using a UPI ID. The app is the interface; UPI is the shared payment arrangement connecting participating institutions.

teacher_understanding.question: What is IMPS, and how is it used?
teacher_understanding.answer: IMPS means Immediate Payment Service. It enables immediate interbank transfers round the clock, such as sending urgent money to a relative through mobile or internet banking. Account number with IFSC is one addressing route; mobile number with MMID is another.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should UPI and IMPS not be treated as identical names for one app?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both support immediate transfers, but they are distinct NPCI services. UPI offers app-based payment initiation using features such as UPI IDs and QR codes; IMPS is a transfer service commonly accessed through bank channels. Neither name denotes just one commercial app.

teacher_understanding.question: What is RuPay, and where is it seen?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay is India's domestic card payment network. A bank can issue a RuPay debit, credit or prepaid card for transactions such as paying at a shop, making an online purchase or using an ATM. RuPay identifies the card network, not the bank account or a particular bank.

teacher_understanding.question: What is AePS, and what problem does it help solve?
teacher_understanding.answer: AePS means Aadhaar Enabled Payment System. It supports basic banking transactions using Aadhaar authentication for an Aadhaar-linked account. For example, a person can withdraw cash through a business correspondent's micro-ATM using supported biometric authentication, without visiting a regular bank branch.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the familiar AePS cash-withdrawal example work?
teacher_understanding.answer: The customer identifies the Aadhaar-linked banking relationship and authenticates at the correspondent's device. After authorisation, the account is debited and the correspondent hands over cash. Aadhaar helps identify and authenticate the transaction; it is not itself an account holding the money.

teacher_understanding.question: What is NACH, and where is it used?
teacher_understanding.answer: NACH means National Automated Clearing House. It supports bulk electronic credits and debits, including periodic payments. Examples include salary or pension credits to many accounts and authorised recurring debits for insurance premiums or loan instalments.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use NACH rather than manually initiate every recurring payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: An institution may need to pay many people or collect repeated payments from many customers. Bulk processing reduces repeated individual instructions; recurring debits operate under customer authorisation through a mandate, not unrestricted permission to take money.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the five systems be distinguished by familiar uses?
teacher_understanding.answer: Think of UPI for app-based instant payments, IMPS for immediate bank transfers, RuPay for card transactions, AePS for Aadhaar-authenticated basic banking, and NACH for bulk or recurring credits and debits. These are distinguishing functions, not rigidly exclusive use categories.

items.exam_note: Match both operator and function. AePS is Aadhaar-authenticated banking, RuPay is a card network, and NACH handles bulk credits as well as debits; do not reduce every NPCI service to a UPI app.
